messages:
kevin_support: Customer (enterprise acct) reports intermittent 401s and 429s when they run a fanout of short prompts + one large 64k context call. Starts around 10:12 PST. They see auth errors mixed with rate-limit.

maria_repro: Can you paste the exact curl they used and the headers from the failing responses?

kevin_support: Pasted below (redacted key). They said it spikes when they prefetch 16 parallel requests against model-rwd-64k and 8 parallel against rwd-32k.

kevin_support: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"model":"rwd-64k","input":"<large context>...","max_tokens":512}'
```

kevin_support: Example headers from a 429: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
x-rw-rpm: 120
x-rw-tpm: 2400
x-rw-limit: model=200rpm,2000tpm,concurrency=16
retry-after: 1

kevin_support: Example 401 immediately after a 429: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized`
www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"

maria_repro: Odd to see 401 mixed in. Could be the client refreshing keys concurrently and hitting an auth bug, or a side-effect of rate-limit/backoff flow. Do we have request ids/trace ids?

kevin_support: They included a trace id on the 429s: `trace_id=tr-9a8b7c`. I pulled logs from the support console and attached a short snippet.

sophia_eng: Jumping in — from infra side, model-rwd-64k has lower RPM and lower concurrency buckets for long-context instances. If they fanout across mixed context-size variants, the backend can reject different requests differently depending on which endpoint/kind of worker picks it up. Also we do have a known edge case where auth-refresh errors surface as 401 after a rejected token refresh during a burst.

oliver_infra: I pulled the backend logs for trace_id=tr-9a8b7c — here's the condensed flow: token validation OK for initial batch, then token refresh call fails to the auth service with 500, client retries -> auth returns 401, while quota controller was returning 429 for model-specific bucket exhaustion. So two independent errors coincidentally interleaved.

oliver_infra: Relevant snippets: ```
[2026-03-10T17:12:05Z] req=tr-9a8b7c model=rwd-64k worker=pool-4 check-quota -> denied: bucket(model=rwd-64k).rpm=195/200
[2026-03-10T17:12:06Z] auth.refresh token_id=tok-abcd -> upstream 500 (timeout)
[2026-03-10T17:12:06Z] req=tr-9a8b7c client-retry -> auth rejected 401
```

maria_repro: Useful. Customer also mentioned billing showed no anomalies and the API key was active. So likely not a billing lockout.

kevin_support: Repro steps customer used: a node script that prefetches contexts and then fires parallel generates: they `Promise.all` across 24 reqs, with no jitter/backoff.

maria_repro: Please ask them to run a controlled repro with our helper script that adds exponential backoff, limited concurrency, and explicit token sanity checks. Example (share snippet):
```js
// quick repro pattern
const pLimit = require('p-limit');
const limit = pLimit(8); // lower concurrency
const calls = Array.from({length:24}).map((_,i)=>limit(()=>fetchGenerate(i)));
await Promise.all(calls);
```

sophia_eng: Notes for support guidance: 1) For rwd-64k we recommend concurrency <= 12 sustained per API key. 2) Maintain separate key/session for prefetch refresh to avoid token refresh storms. 3) Add randomized jitter on startup to avoid burst aligning with customer's cron. 4) Prefer streaming or incremental context fetch where possible.

kevin_support: Can we confirm the exact per-model published limits to give to the customer? They asked for numbers for RPM, TPM, and concurrency for rwd-64k and rwd-32k.

oliver_infra: Current soft limits (as of deployment): rwd-64k => RPM=200, TPM=2000, concurrency=16 (recommended sustained 12). rwd-32k => RPM=600, TPM=6000, concurrency=48. Important: TPM includes tokens for both context and generated tokens; long-context calls consume a lot of TPM quickly.

maria_repro: Also note burst window: the token bucket allows short bursts but sustained high-RPM across many keys or fanout will hit controller and start returning 429s. If they prefetch many large contexts then try to generate, they'll exhaust TPM fast.

kevin_support: Customer ran `--context-length` ~58k tokens for rwd-64k calls. That alone eats ~58k of their TPM per request. With 16 parallel requests that would be ~928k tokens counted quickly — explains hitting TPM.

oliver_infra: Exactly. TPM=2000 in our header is in token units x1000? (internal scaling) but short answer: their traffic pattern is TPM-bound.

maria_repro: Action items for support to ask customer to try now: 1) Reduce parallelism to 8 and add jitter. 2) Run the repro with a fresh API key to rule out auth-refresh storm. 3) Send a curl that includes `X-Rw-Client-Trace: <id>` so we can map traces. 4) If they need sustained throughput for large contexts, recommend Dedicated plan.

kevin_support: I shared a one-line mitigation: "reduce concurrent rwd-64k calls to <=8, add backoff jitter, and rotate token if you see 401s after 429" — they tried and saw 429 frequency drop, 401s stopped.

sophia_eng: For follow-up, I'll open an infra ticket to harden auth refresh under quota-denied flows (so 401s don't cascade during bursts). I'll also run a short synthetic load against the model to validate controller behavior.

oliver_infra: Filed infra ticket INF-2026-317 with notes and attached traces. Marking for oncall to verify the auth refresh retry circuit.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-317 (assigned to oliver_infra) :red_circle:

kevin_support: Marking the customer sequence as resolved for now; they'll consider Dedicated. I'll follow up if they opt in. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sophia_eng: TL;DR for support reply to customer: "You're hitting the token-per-minute (TPM) bucket due to many large-context requests + fanout; reduce concurrency and add jitter. The 401s were caused by concurrent token refresh failures during the burst — we've opened an infra ticket to prevent that. If you need sustained large-context capacity, we recommend Dedicated capacity."

kevin_support: Closing thread once we get customer confirmation they moved to safe pattern.
